keyVerseText: And he sent by the hand of Nathan the prophet; and he called his name Jedidiah, because of the LORD. Jedidiah: that is, Beloved of the LORD
rootMeaning: The name יְדִידְיָה (Yᵉdîydᵉyâh) derives from the root יְדִיד (yᵉdîyd), meaning 'beloved' or 'amiable,' combined with the divine element יָהּ (Yah), a shortened form of Yahweh. Thus, the literal meaning is 'beloved of Yahweh' or 'beloved of Jehovah.' This etymology emphasizes a personal and affectionate relationship with God, going beyond the general English gloss by highlighting the intimate bond between the individual and the divine.
usageInScripture: The term יְדִידְיָה appears only once in Scripture, specifically as a proper name given to Solomon by the prophet Nathan. It is consistently translated as 'Jedidiah,' underscoring its status as a unique, divinely bestowed name. This singular usage reflects its special significance as a title that affirms Solomon's beloved status before the LORD, rather than a common noun or adjective used broadly.
theologicalSignificance: The name יְדִידְיָה reveals profound theological truth about God's love and favor. By naming Solomon 'beloved of Jehovah,' God publicly affirms His special love and covenantal relationship with Solomon despite the surrounding circumstances. This highlights how divine love is not merely abstract but is personally directed and expressed toward individuals chosen for His purposes. For the Christian faith, this points forward to the ultimate beloved Son, Jesus Christ, who is uniquely loved by the Father and through whom believers share in that divine affection.
keyVerseReflection: 2 Samuel 12:25 states, 'And he sent by the hand of Nathan the prophet; and he called his name Jedidiah, because of the LORD. Jedidiah: that is, Beloved of the LORD.' This verse emphasizes that the name Jedidiah was divinely given, signifying God’s affectionate favor upon Solomon. The word יְדִידְיָה here deepens the understanding of Solomon’s identity as not only a royal heir but also as one specially loved and appointed by God, a reminder of God’s sovereign grace in leadership and covenant.
